says: In next/, the saved-table guard (refold when the entry at the saved rev is gone or changed) is reached by no law on its own: with it switched off, both ProcessManagerMemo laws pass, because only a save made after an append can make it matter, and no law draws a ledger rewrite below the saved rev.
proof: Scratch worktree at caa79fedc: replacing `if (kept === undefined || !sameEntry(kept, entry))` with `if (false)` and running `vitest run --maxWorkers=1 next/packages/libfabrika/src/processes/ProcessManagerMemo.test.ts` printed `Tests 2 passed (2)`; with `table(turn)` also made to save its fold, it printed `Tests 1 failed | 1 passed (2)`.
cost: A later change that lets a fold after an append be saved, or a ledger rewrite, would rely on a guard whose own break no law turns red.
